About the role At AlayaCare, we are transforming how work gets done for the AI era by redesigning our end-to-end processes around the outcomes they deliver. As AI Transformation Lead, Marketing, you will lead this work for the processes that start in or run through Marketing, so they deliver better results more efficiently and with fewer handoffs. You will report to the AI Transformation Manager, Commercial, and partner with Marketing leaders and the adjacent teams in Sales and Product. You will use a Lean, outcome-first approach to define what each process should deliver, measure the current state, design the simplest future state, build and pilot it, and prove the result against the baseline. You will partner with each function's embedded data and AI specialist, who supplies the data and KPIs and tracks results once a redesign is adopted. Where you will focus Your initial focus will include the processes below. As you work with Marketing leaders across our markets, you will also identify and prioritize new opportunities as they emerge. Campaign to qualified pipeline: how campaigns, content and lead generation turn into sales-qualified opportunities, including the handoff to Sales. Content request to published asset: how content is briefed, drafted, reviewed for brand and accuracy, approved and published. Market insight to positioning: how market, competitive and regulatory intelligence becomes positioning, messaging and input to product and go-to-market decisions. Market change to sales readiness: how market and regulatory changes become approved talk tracks, battlecards and answers that customer-facing teams use. Product release to adoption: how releases are launched, communicated and adopted by internal teams and customers. Your scope can grow as the business's needs and your skills develop. What you will do Assess and define: evaluate opportunities with business leaders, then agree on the outcome and key metrics with the executive sponsor. Map and analyze: map how the work happens today with the people who do it, baseline its performance, and find the waste and its root causes. Design and make the case: design a simpler process that removes unnecessary steps and handoffs, using automation and AI where they add value, and build the business case for leadership approval. Build, pilot and measure: build and pilot solutions hands-on with AI tools, measure results against the baseline, and recommend whether to adopt, refine or roll back. Lead the change: bring leaders and teams along so the new way of working sticks, and scale what works. What success looks like First month: your first process has a defined outcome, a mapped current state and a baseline signed off by its sponsor. First quarter: future-state designs approved and at least two processes in pilot, with measurable efficiency gains realized. Solutions that work: every tool you build moves the process's primary KPI, saves time and cost, is easy for teams to adopt, is secure and doesn't add complexity. What this role does not own Selecting company-wide tools and platforms, which the central tooling team owns. Production engineering and long-term maintenance, which Engineering and IT own. Security, privacy and compliance sign-off; you design to these requirements and involve reviewers early. Ongoing reporting once a process is handed over, which the function's data and AI partners own. What you bring Marketing experience: Hands-on experience in at least one core B2B marketing function: product marketing, demand generation, content marketing or marketing operations. Working knowledge of the marketing funnel and its metrics, such as MQL-to-SQL conversion, pipeline contribution, campaign ROI, content velocity and launch adoption. Experience with CRM and marketing automation platforms such as HubSpot and Semrush, and comfort pulling and interpreting their data. We are building a team of full-stack people, where each person brings together three skill sets: Process improvement: mapping end-to-end processes, finding waste and designing simpler ways of working (for example Lean, value stream mapping or business process redesign). Change and people: bringing leaders and teams along, working through competing priorities and making change stick. Solution building: turning a redesigned process into working agents, automations and tools. You configure and connect AI tools yourself: building agents and prompts, linking workflows through automation platforms, APIs or MCP servers, and using light scripting or SQL to pull and test data. You can judge whether an output is reliable enough to trust and know when a solution should go to Engineering or IT to harden. We don't expect you to be an expert in everything. efficient end to end solutions for complex business problems •Apply architectural and engineering concepts to design solutions that meet operational requirements, such as scalability, maintainability, security, reliability, extensibility, flexibility, availability, and manageability. •Manage the technical delivery of custom development integrations and data migration elements of a Salesforce com implementation •Technical Strategy Development: Develop and execute a comprehensive technical strategy for Salesforce platform encompassing architecture design development integration and maintenance •Conduct research and develop Proof of Concepts on emerging technologies and implementation toolkits in support of anticipated development efforts and recommend technologies that are functionally robust and cost effective. •Research, enforce, and drive the adoption of design patterns throughout the enterprise and evangelize standard processes for solution design and development. •Contribute to producing target state solution architectures, conducting architectural assessments and gap analyses, and shaping the overall solution strategy and roadmap •Partner with data architect(s) to support data management practices, ensuring data integrity, security, and compliance •Partner with integration architect(s) to support integration strategies ensuring seamless communication and data flow across various systems •Work closely with solution architects to ensure that individual solutions align with the overall enterprise architecture •Collaborate with business leaders to create business capability models that align technology capabilities with business needs •Contribute to building a vibrant ‘learning community’ within the enterprise architecture discipline, fostering continuous improvement and consistently delivering value to various business units Required Experience & Skills: •Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer science, Information Technology, or a related field •5+ years of experience as a senior domain architect or senior enterprise architect. •Prior experience as a Principal Salesforce Architect in a global organization working with Salesforce Connected Apps (applications from SalesForce App Exchange) •Proven experience designing and delivering complex B2B SaaS Salesforce solutions. •Led at least two large-scale Product-to-Cash (CPQ/RCA) implementations Salesforce architecture capabilities and ecosystem including Sales Cloud Service Cloud Marketing Cloud and Community Cloud or SuccessFactors ecosystem. •Strong leadership and interpersonal skills with the ability to effectively communicate complex technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders •Salesforce certifications such as Salesforce Certified Technical Architect CTA Salesforce Certified Application Architect or Salesforce Certified System Architect preferred •5 years of Hands-on enterprise architecture framework experience (TOGAF, C4, Archimate etc.) •Strong analytical, problem-solving, communication skills •Previous roles with a focus on data architecture, application or solution architecture, integration, risk management, and technology standards •

ABOUT AUGUST HEALTH

At August Health, our mission is to empower the essential work of caring for our elders.

We achieve this by providing a modern operating platform and electronic health record (EHR) that enables senior living operators to deliver high-quality care with confidence.

Caregivers are the heart of senior living communities, embodying care, compassion, and well-being. Yet, they face increasing challenges—higher resident acuity, complex workflows, and staffing shortages. At August Health, we build tools that simplify their tasks, eliminate inefficiencies, and provide the insights they need to focus on what truly matters—caring for residents.

At August, we strive to live our values each day, in every interaction with our customers and with each other.

 - Be responsible – leave things better than you found them

 - Take ownership – be decisive and take action

 - Be ambitious – build something great

 - Keep an open mindset – communicate candidly and welcome new ideas

 - Be humble – celebrate each others’ successes and learn from our mistakes

 - Stay positive – assume best intent




ABOUT THE ROLE

At August, data is one of the biggest reasons customers choose us. Everyone who uses August, from caregivers to executives, relies on data to do their job, and their needs keep growing. We’re looking for a Senior Data Analyst to set the standard for how August turns customer data into insights that drive action.

You’ll build the metrics, reports, and models behind our Insights product, helping senior living operators understand their performance and spot problems early. Working with Product, Engineering, and Customer Success, you’ll show communities how data can simplify workflows, reduce administrative burden, and free caregivers to focus on resident care.




WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Turn recurring questions into scalable, self-serve reporting so customers and internal teams can find answers without an analyst

 - Define and own metrics that help senior living leaders understand performance and compare across communities, regions, and teams

 - Build and improve data models that connect information across our products and hold up over time

 - Explore trends, patterns, and predictive opportunities in our data, and turn findings into insights customers can act on

 - Partner with Product and Engineering to shape our Insights roadmap and bring data into the product itself

 - Help find new ways for insights to reach people where they work

 - Partner with Customer Success on customer conversations and QBRs, presenting findings as clear, actionable recommendations

 - Scope ambiguous questions from leadership and Customer Success into structured analyses with minimal direction

 - Raise the bar for data quality, documentation, and analytics practices across the team




ABOUT YOU

 - 6+ years of experience as a data analyst, with advanced SQL and database skills

 - Experience writing transformation logic and data pipelines

 - Experience designing data models and metrics that stay accurate over time, not just one-off queries

 - A track record of independently owning analytics projects from ambiguous question to shipped insight

 - Solid understanding of statistics, with some experience building or applying forecasting or predictive models

 - Experience building self-serve reporting with BI tools such as Omni, Looker, or similar

 - Experience presenting to external stakeholders and working directly with customers

 - Strong understanding of data privacy and responsible data stewardship

 - Excellent communication skills: you can make complex data accessible to anyone

 - Healthcare data experience (EHR systems, clinical data, medical terminology) is a plus; senior living experience is a bonus




ABOUT OUR TEAM

Our team brings together deep expertise in technology, healthcare, and company-building. We’ve led teams at Apple, Google, Landmark Health, and Adobe, co-founded and exited multiple companies, shipped products used by hundreds of millions of users, and managed clinical teams caring for thousands of patients.

Backed by top-tier Silicon Valley investors, we are partnering with some of the largest senior care organizations in the U.S. to transform the future of senior living.

We offer market-competitive compensation based on experience and ability, including significant equity option grants. Our benefits prioritize your well-being with 100% company-paid premiums for health, dental, and vision coverage, along with company contributions to your HSA. We help you plan for the future with a 2% 401(k) match, and support your physical and mental health through services like Rightway Health Advocacy and Spring Health Mental Wellness. Beyond traditional benefits, we offer a flexible time off policy, 100% paid family leave, and all-expenses-paid, in-person company offsites twice a year.

At its core, enhanced housing with services is a proactive approach wherein resident services staff regularly and actively reach out to each individual resident to engage with them around their health and wellness, identify areas of need/risk and provide intensive, individualized case management and support as needed and desired by the resident. The Wellness Coordinator (WC) serves a lead role in the R3 Initiative engaging residents in wellness assessments and health education programs, connecting residents to needed services, providing a wide variety of case management tasks, coordinating activities with the Nurse Care Manager, and ensuring that all interventions are documented and tracked. This role requires a leader with a flexible, can-do attitude. The Wellness Coordinator is directly responsible for assuring that there is excellent communication and coordination with all team members and local providers to support residents in living independently and safely for as long as possible. Please note that this location is T accessible; there is no parking available. II. Core Competencies: Commit to the organization’s core values of respect, dignity and empowerment. Able to form trusting relationships with residents, families, and team members. Work collaboratively with colleagues, both within and outside the HSL continuum. Listen attentively; speak respectfully; maintain confidentiality. Provide the highest quality of preparation and presentation. Have a “can-do” service mentality. Accept responsibility for all tasks assigned. Work independently toward achieving program goals III. Position Responsibilities: Partner with the Nurse Care Manager and the resident services team to provide comprehensive case management services to residents. Provide regular preventative outreach to all residents to check in on their needs and overall health and develop trusting relationships with residents and their families. Conduct wellness assessments of residents to determine needs and goals; develop wellness plans addressing physical, social, cognitive, spiritual and mental health domains. Actively follow up on all identified needs including finding resources, making referrals and ensuring residents are actively engaged in services. Coordinate with primary care physicians, mental health providers and hospitals. Ensure effective communication around changes in status, transitions and service utilization. Active follow up on all hospitalizations, rehab stays, emergency room visits. Work with families, hospitals, rehabs, HSL Home Care and/or VNA, ASAP’s and other providers to ensure safe discharges and ongoing services. Occasional translation or interpretation as needed. Partner with housing staff to tailor programming that meets resident needs. Educate housing staff members including office, maintenance, housekeeping, programming. and dietary staff to identify and communicate concerning changes in residents’ condition. Coordinate with residents to complete files including important health care information, end of life planning, and emergency contacts. Support on site services and connection to required off site services by following up with at risk residents to ensure adherence to health and wellness related activities. Develop relationships with all payers serving seniors in the sites. Implement effective communication systems between housing and providers to relay important information (changes in condition, transitions between settings, changes in behavior/activity). Promote self-care among residents through individualized coaching to identify personal goals and implement programs and services that support those goals as well as coordinate with care providers. Partner with and make referrals to all appropriate local service providers, for example: Visiting Nurses Associations, ASAP’s, Rehabilitation Services, PACE Programs, Adult Day Health Programs, Memory Evaluation Programs, etc. Participate and/or lead care planning meetings at the housing site. Assess the needs of residents with dementia and make appropriate referrals as needed. Work with local hospitals, HSL Home Care and/or VNA case management to ensure safe discharges with appropriate service coordination. Assist residents with transition to other levels of care as needed; conduct family meetings and attend off-site team meetings when necessary to coordinate care and discharge planning needs. Offer advocacy for residents and serve as a liaison for families. Coordinate and participate in the tracking of metrics/measures as well as the creation of reports on outcomes. As needed, support team members with tasks, including room set-up, or photocopying materials. IV. Qualifications: Masters degree in social work or a human service field and 1-2 years of experience working as a case manager or care coordinator in aging services strongly preferred; Bachelor’s degree with 3-5 years experience required. Must have compassion for and a desire to work with a senior population. Excellent organization and interpersonal skills, including the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously, work efficiently and proactively as part of a team. Excellent oral and written communication skills, including ability to communicate with residents, families and team members in a manner that conveys respects, caring and sensitivity. Must be a professional, proactive, collaborative, conscientious, and results-oriented individual. Must have an optimistic and positive demeanor, , good intuition and sound judgment. Brings a solution-focused attitude to addressing challenges. Must be motivated to learn and flexible to change; open to feedback. Must be able to collect needed information and document clearly in AASC Online software. Computer literacy; experience with Windows, Word, Power Point, and Excel Some travel in the Boston metro area for site visits and meetings is required. Certification in Dementia Care preferred. Fluency in Cantonese required; Mandarin a plus V. Physical Requirements: Must be able to lift, push and pull 25 pounds. Must be able to stand, walk, drive and sit during scheduled work times. Job Summary The Harvard Pilgrim Health Care Institute, a research and teaching collaboration between Harvard Pilgrim Health Care and Harvard Medical School is looking for a Director of Research Computing, Data & Technology. The Director of Research Computing, Data & Technology reports to the Vice President, Administration and Finance at the Harvard Pilgrim Health Care Institute (Institute). This role works closely with Institute leadership, faculty investigators, research center directors, research administration, compliance, privacy, security, and enterprise IT partners. This individual is responsible for developing and executing the Institute's research technology strategy and oversight of research computing, research technology, data enablement, and related support staff. The role combines strategic planning, innovation leadership, stakeholder engagement, governance, and program management with a deep understanding of research operations and scientific workflows. The Director serves as the primary liaison among researchers, operational leadership, enterprise IT, compliance, and external partners to ensure that technology investments align with scientific priorities and institutional objectives. The position directly supervises a team of four and is expected to provide leadership and oversight for research technology initiatives, including evaluating and, where warranted, redesigning the roles, structure, and responsibilities of this team to align with the Institute's research technology strategy. Job Description Key Responsibilties/Duties: Provide strategic leadership and maintain a multi-year roadmap for research computing, data management, analytics, AI, and digital research enablement. Lead and develop the research technology team by optimizing organizational structure, setting goals, coaching staff, and managing performance. Serve as a trusted advisor to researchers and Institute leadership, aligning technology initiatives with scientific, operational, and strategic priorities. Translate research requirements into scalable, secure, and innovative technology solutions while serving as the primary liaison between researchers and enterprise IT. Drive digital transformation through automation, cloud services, advanced analytics, AI, and emerging technologies to enhance research productivity and innovation. Oversee all Institute computing and data storage environments, including cloud platforms, servers, research computing resources, and shared network drives. Direct the governance and lifecycle management of Institute data assets, including acquisition, contracting, data sharing agreements, onboarding/offboarding processes, SOPs, retention, and secure destruction. Provide shared oversight of Research Service Data Center (RSDC) technical environments and serve as the primary liaison for related partnerships, governance, and data-sharing agreements. Oversee Institute-approved software assets, including vendor management, contracting, licensing, distribution, compliance, and lifecycle management. Establish governance, compliance, and policy frameworks that balance innovation, security, regulatory requirements, and responsible research practices. Manage the research technology portfolio, budget, performance metrics, and strategic reporting, including tracking utilization of data assets to support grant, contract, and funding opportunities. Core Competencies Strategic vision and execution; technology innovation and digital transformation; research operations expertise. Stakeholder engagement and influence; program and portfolio management; change leadership; team leadership and organizational design. Governance and policy development; financial and resource planning; partnership development; executive communication. Education, Certification and Licensure Master's degree in informatics, data science, public health, health services research, computer science, healthcare analytics, business, or a related field. Experience (Minimum years required): Eight to ten years of progressively responsible leadership experience in research technology, research administration, research computing, informatics, or related areas, including five to seven years in management or supervisory capacity. Demonstrated success leading cross-functional initiatives involving researchers, technology teams, and organizational leadership. Strong understanding of research workflows, sponsored research, and technology-enabled scientific collaboration. Exceptional communication, facilitation, and stakeholder management skills. Skill Requirements: Working knowledge of research computing and data platforms, including cloud computing, high-performance computing, and analytics environments. Familiarity with AI-enabled research tools and emerging technologies, and their practical application to scientific workflows. Knowledge of research data governance, privacy, and security requirements, including IRB, HIPAA, and sponsor data use obligations. Skilled in project and portfolio management, including budgeting, resource planning, and performance measurement. Proven ability to build consensus and influence stakeholders across research, technical, and administrative functions without direct authority. Job Summary Reporting to the Director of Risk Adjustment Reporting and Analytics, the Manager of Reporting and Analytics – Medicare Advantage will apply a blend of advanced business, analytical, technical, and leadership skills to ensure the accuracy, completeness, and integrity of risk adjustment data submissions to CMS. This role will optimize risk score accuracy, support revenue performance across all Medicare Advantage products, and ensure the timely, accurate, and compliant submission and reporting of All-Payer Claims Database (APCD) files to six state agencies. This individual will synthesize large data sets, complex information and work effectively across business areas including Member Operations, Provider Information, Claims, Information Technology (IT) and Actuarial. The Manager will possess a strong understanding of data architecture, data lineage, and relational databases and will actively partner with IT teams on solution design, data flow analysis, root-cause investigations, implementation planning, and quality assurance of IT deliverables. The Manager will lead a team of 3-4 senior analysts and data leads, providing coaching, mentorship, performance management, and professional development to build a highly engaged and high-performing team. In addition, the Manager will oversee all EDS/EDPS submissions for Point32Health and serve as the organization's subject matter expert for Medicare Advantage Encounter Data Processing System (EDS/EDPS) submissions and APCD reporting. Job Description Key Responsibilities/Duties – what you will be doing (top five): 1. Medicare Advantage and APCD Data Governance, Reporting, and Submission Oversight: Be responsible for the planning, execution, program implementation, and monitoring of Medicare Advantage and All-Payer Claims Database (APCD) data submission and reporting efforts. Regularly review the effectiveness, accuracy, and compliance of claims, supplemental data, and APCD submission processes, infrastructure, and reporting; recommend design enhancements and implement changes as needed. Oversee the maintenance of data controls, dashboard reporting, and routine data reconciliations, and provide regular updates to management. Routinely present key issues, business updates, and performance metrics related to Medicare Advantage risk adjustment. 2. Collaboration and Stakeholder Management: Collaborate closely with Actuarial on Medicare Advantage analytics, program, and provider-level analyses, and targeting. Partner with internal stakeholders, including Claims, Membership Operations, Provider Information, External Vendors, and IT, to ensure that process enhancements and data management mechanisms are developed, maintained, and monitored on an ongoing basis. Lead communication, coordination, issue resolution, and compliance-related activities with six state agencies related to All-Payer Claims Database (APCD) submissions, ensuring timely, accurate, and compliant reporting. Participate in and contribute to strategic planning efforts and annual risk adjustment business plan development. Participate in CMS and industry calls and monitor changes in regulations and technical specifications affecting EDS/EDPS and APCD submissions. Serve as the organization's subject matter expert for EDS/EDPS (Encounter Data Processing System) and APCD reporting requirements, both internally and in interactions with CMS and state regulatory agencies. 3. Data Optimization, Submissions, and Integrity: Oversee data management and submission responsibilities for EDS/EDPS CMS submissions for Massachusetts HMO, PPO, SCO, Unify products and Connecticut HMO and PPO products, as well as All-Payer Claims Database (APCD) submissions to six state agencies. Ensure timely, complete, accurate, and compliant data submissions and reporting. Review CMS-reported errors, outliers, and data quality findings, and collaborate with Actuarial, IT, Operational, and vendor partners to remediate issues, implement corrective actions, or provide appropriate justification. Coordinate all required reviews and sign-offs for EDS/EDPS and APCD submissions. Develop internal capabilities and/or partner with vendors to support data optimization efforts, maintaining a catalog of data quality, operational efficiency, and submission enhancement opportunities. Participate, as required, in corporate project and strategic initiatives, including the development, evaluation, and presentation of business cases related to EDS/EDPS, APCD, and data optimization efforts. Oversee and monitor the processes for accepting, submitting, reconciling, and accurately tracking all supplemental submissions and deletes. Review and assess CMS HPMS memoranda and related regulatory guidance, identify operational and reporting impacts, and partner with internal stakeholders to ensure timely implementation of required actions, process changes, and compliance obligations 4. Analytics and Reporting: Coordinate with vendors and/or Actuarial teams to ensure that accurate and complete data is utilized for valuation, forecasting, targeting, and performance analyses supporting Medicare Advantage products. Manage and perform data analytics to support ongoing and emerging risk adjustment initiatives. Build, maintain, and enhance EDS/EDPS tieback processes and reporting for actuarial valuation exercises. Develop executive-level reports, dashboards, and PowerPoint presentations that clearly communicate reconciliation results, key findings, risks, opportunities, and recommendations. 5. General Management: The Manager will lead a team of 3-4 FTEs, including senior analysts and data leads, providing coaching, mentorship, performance management, and professional development to foster a high-performing team. This role is responsible for reviewing analytics, reporting, documentation, and technical deliverables to ensure quality, accuracy, and alignment with business objectives. Job Summary Harvard Pilgrim Health Care Institute is currently seeking a highly motivated individual to join our organization as SAS Programmer, who will work collaboratively with investigators, statisticians, and senior programmers. The SAS Programmer will work within the Division of Health Policy and Insurance Research (HPI) within the Department of Population Medicine (DPM). The SAS Programmer will perform a variety of activities to support the project team, including assisting with data cleaning, database development, dataset creation, software programming, data management, statistical analysis, and results reporting for internal and external research projects. The individual will primarily work with large health insurance claims data (e.g., CMS Medicaid claims data, All Payer Claims Data) under the direction of a senior programmer and project manager. The SAS programmer will work across a multi-project research portfolio examining effects of health policies on health outcomes, including work focused on maternal health, child health, and mental health. Their work will be done in collaboration with the larger research team, which includes health services researchers, biostatisticians, clinicians, economists, and epidemiologists. WHO WE ARE The Department of Population Medicine (DPM) is a research and teaching collaboration between Harvard Medical School (HMS) and Harvard Pilgrim Health Care. Our mission is to improve health care delivery and population health through research and education, in partnership with health plans, delivery systems, and public health agencies. As the nation’s first medical school appointing department based in a health plan, we are strategically positioned to improve population health and health care delivery locally, nationally, and internationally. DPM is home to five divisions and six Centers of Excellence, which facilitate collaborations across divisions. Researchers in DPM work closely with other Harvard faculty at HMS, at the Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health, and across the University, as well as many health systems, hospitals, and community partners. The Division of Health Policy and Insurance Research (HPI) is one of five divisions within DPM. Our researchers study state and federal policies, payment and insurance reforms, care delivery models, and digital health innovations – with a focus on both commercial (employer sponsored insurance, Marketplace) and public (Medicaid, Medicare) populations and payers – in core areas of: pharmaceutical policy and systems, maternal and child health, mental health and substance use, chronic disease, cancer, and health care workforce. We do so using quasi-experimental and other health services research methods, with large administrative data sources (claims data, EHR data, survey data), with an overarching focus on access, quality, affordability, and equity of care for marginalized populations. We work in close collaboration with local, national, and international partners. WHAT YOU WILL BE DOING • Use SAS software to clean, quality check, and troubleshoot health insurance claims data • Design, develop, test, execute, and maintain SAS programs to create cohorts and generate variables • Create and maintain analytic datasets using raw data files, including complex data linkages, merging, and transformation workflows • Generate descriptive data and conduct statistical analyses, in close consultation with investigators, statisticians, and senior programmers • Use Excel or other programs to display user-friendly results in graphical or numerical form • Utilize knowledge of analytic and statistical concepts, techniques, and methods in daily work • Participate in project meetings, both via telephone and in-person • Contribute to the development of manuscripts and reports • Perform out-of-the-box thinking, collaborate with others, and make a difference every day! QUALIFICATIONS REQUIRED • Bachelor’s Degree (BA, BS) • At least 2 years of full-time work as a programmer or equivalent SAS programming experience, including macro programming and PROC SQL • Experience transforming and analyzing large administrative health care data, including claims data (such as CMS Medicaid or Medicare claims, all-payer claims databases, commercial claims) • Experience with epidemiologic and biostatistics principles and methods • Ability to prioritize work, operate under tight deadlines, and meet deadlines • Proficiency with software packages, including Microsoft Office suite (e.g., Excel) • Excellent organizational skills, accuracy, and attention to detail. • Resilient, collaborative, flexible, and independent PREFERRED • Master's Degree in Public Health, Epidemiology, Biostatistics, Statistics, or another health-related field • Programming experience in at least one other programming language (e.g., Stata, R) • Knowledge of health care systems, health care delivery, or health policy • Experience with, and understanding of, claims-related elements such as ICD diagnosis codes and procedure codes • Experience conducting regression analyses WHAT MAKES US STAND OUT • Work-Life-Flexibility • Paid volunteer time off (up to 3 days annually) • Open Time Off • Annual Mini-Grant of $500 donated to a non-profit organization of the employee’s choice • Educational Reimbursement WORKING ENVIRONMENT Hybrid office environment based in Boston, MA. The Senior AI & Automation Engineer is a senior individual contributor and technical leader on the Data & Technology Solutions team, responsible for architecting, building, and scaling intelligent AI systems and enterprise automation solutions that directly improve care quality and operational performance across our Medicare Advantage business. You will serve as a go-to technical expert for AI Scientists, Data Engineers, Product Managers, Clinical Operations, and Application Engineering teams — driving end-to-end delivery of production AI systems that span claims processing, risk adjustment, prior authorization, revenue integrity, and member engagement. This role carries a higher degree of independent ownership and technical authority than the mid-level equivalent, with expectations to lead complex, ambiguous initiatives from concept through production and to actively elevate the engineering practices of the broader team. Lead the build of distributed, cloud-native systems for enterprise workloads. Own the design and build of services, APIs, and microservices that run reliably at scale in a regulated environment. Set the standard for distributed systems practice on the team: fault tolerance, retries and idempotency, queuing and eventing, caching, and horizontal scaling. Lead hybrid infrastructure work bridging cloud and non-cloud systems. Own the build of integrations with non-API data sources, including flat files, legacy databases, EDI feeds, mainframes, and streaming data, as well as multimodal data such as documents, images, and audio. Set integration patterns the rest of the team builds against. Own CI/CD, containerization, and deployment standards. Drive adoption of Docker, Kubernetes, and CI/CD best practices across the team. Own infrastructure-as-code standards for the systems the team builds. Own data and automation pipeline reliability. Build and govern ETL and orchestration pipelines at scale. Own automation strategy using RPA platforms and orchestration tools, including ROI governance and engineering standards for fault-tolerant workflow design. Apply AI/ML to production systems and own inferencing performance (applied, not research). Own the build of inferencing pipelines (batch, real-time, streaming) that serve models handed off from AI Sciences, for workloads such as claims processing, risk adjustment, and member communication. Partner directly with AI Scientists to take models from research into low-latency, high-throughput production systems, owning the benchmarking and tuning that gets them there. This is applied integration, serving, and performance ownership, not model research or training. The Incident Response Analyst is responsible for first-line monitoring, triage, detection, and escalation of security alerts and reported phishing activity across the organization's information systems. The role works under general direction, exercising independent judgment on day-to-day disposition and containment decisions, and collaborates closely with Information Security staff, IT Operations, and Compliance stakeholders to protect sensitive Medicare Advantage member data under HIPAA and HITRUST regulatory frameworks. By owning high-volume alert triage, limited containment actions, and structured incident documentation, this position directly reduces risk exposure and supports audit readiness, while building a clear, reviewable record of progression toward threat hunting and broader detection engineering over time. Job Duties / Responsibilities Triage and Investigate Security Alerts. Monitor and disposition alerts from the endpoint detection and response (EDR) platform, applying judgment to determine which investigative path to follow and how deeply to investigate within documented escalation criteria, and recording the specific process, file, or network activity reviewed and the reasoning behind each disposition, not only the outcome. Respond to and Contain Confirmed Threats. Independently assess evidence of compromise and, when warranted, restrict or disable a host or account without waiting for approval, then promptly notify senior Information Security staff of the action taken and the rationale. Investigate and Triage Phishing Reports. Independently determine whether a reported or suspicious email is malicious or benign, using the organization's email security platform to validate sender reputation, headers, and links, and take appropriate action, recognizing that an incorrect disposition carries real consequences for member data and organizational integrity. Query and Correlate Logs in the SIEM. Independently query and correlate logs in the organization's SIEM or log-analytics platform to support alert triage, incident investigation, and ad hoc security requests from Information Security leadership. Apply Threat Intelligence to Detection and Blocking. Monitor threat-intelligence feeds and healthcare sector ISACs for indicators of compromise, and add confirmed malicious indicators to blocklists directly; propose broader architectural tuning changes to senior staff for review. This foundation is expected to grow into independently proposing and implementing more complex, cross-system tuning and control changes over time, documented to provide a clear, reviewable record of progression. Tune Detection Rules and Suppress False Positives. Implement narrowly scoped tuning changes to the EDR and SIEM (e.g., suppressing a confirmed false positive or adjusting a basic detection rule for a confirmed pattern), documenting each change and building, with increasing independence over time, toward structured, hypothesis-driven threat hunting during low-volume periods, providing a clear, reviewable record of progression along this path. Document Incidents and Escalate with Clarity. Document all incidents and investigations using the team's incident-tracking system and NIST SP 800-61 methodology, providing factual, auditable detail and a reasoned recommendation that senior staff rely on whenever escalating. Maintain Compliance Awareness and Regulatory Currency. Stay current on HIPAA, HITRUST, the NIST Cybersecurity Framework, and CIS Controls as they apply to day-to-day triage work, performing all work in an ethical manner consistent with contractual, regulatory, and legal obligations. Respond to After-Hours Critical Alerts. Respond to occasional after-hours security alerts that are critical in nature, following defined escalation procedures. Triage and Route Incoming Tickets. Perform first-pass normalization, triage, and routing of incoming Information Security tickets, treating every new ticket as a potential availability-impacting issue until triage determines otherwise, and assign each ticket to the appropriate Information Security staff member in a timely manner. Participate in Team Operations. Participate in Information Security team stand-ups, tabletop exercises, and periodic peer review of closed tickets. Demonstrated ability to independently query and correlate logs in a SIEM or log-analytics platform to support an investigation. Demonstrated ability to evaluate evidence of compromise and decide, without waiting for approval, whether to restrict or disable a host or account, weighing the consequence of acting against the consequence of not acting. Clover Health is investing in our fraud detection and investigation capabilities and is seeking a Director, AI-Enabled Fraud Prevention & Investigations to join our Legal department as a senior individual contributor. This hybrid role combines: (1) managing hands-on investigations of potential provider fraud with (2) building AI-powered tools and processes to make investigations more efficient and help catch potential future fraud earlier. You will develop and pilot new AI-enabled investigatory processes for Clover’s Medicare Advantage business, and own resulting investigations, in collaboration with Clover’s Special Investigations Unit (SIU) and other stakeholders. This is a non-attorney role. You will work hand-in-hand with Clover’s lawyers and SIU to ensure that new investigatory processes you develop, and the resulting investigations, comply with Clover policies and regulatory requirements. Success in this role requires someone sharp, creative, and technically hands-on—someone who does not just use existing analytics tools but builds their own. That might mean writing a script to automate repetitive work, pulling apart a dataset when a standard report falls short, or working with an LLM until it produces something genuinely useful—all with the goal of finding smarter, more effective ways to investigate potential provider fraud. As a Director, AI-Enabled Fraud Prevention & Investigations, you will: Build Your Own Investigative Tooling: Use AI to write the queries, scripts, and prompts that turn millions of claim lines and/or medical record data into a prioritized list of leads. Prototype detection logic yourself rather than waiting on a roadmap, and hand off what works to data science and engineering to productionize. We expect you to be the person who builds v1. Investigate Potential Fraud End-to-End With AI in the Loop: Own a portfolio of fraud investigations sourced using the tooling you develop, in collaboration with Clover’s SIU. Develop investigative plans, gather and analyze evidence (including claims data and medical records), and reach well-supported conclusions. Use LLMs and analytics to compress the parts of an investigation that have always been slow — reading unstructured data, triaging grievance narratives, and sizing exposure. Build Defensible Documentation: Develop case files and memos that are factually complete, well-organized, and prepared with the evidentiary and procedural standards necessary for downstream enforcement, recoveries, or provider actions. Collaborate Across Functions: Work with Clover's clinical, compliance, claims, payment integrity, provider relations, revenue operations, and SIU teams to gather information, validate findings, and translate investigative outcomes into operational improvements, provider education, and member impact. Communicate Findings Clearly: Prepare concise written reports and oral briefings that translate complex investigative facts into clear narratives for senior leadership and other stakeholders. Success in this role looks like: In your first 90 days , you have embedded yourself as a trusted partner to both the Legal department and Clover’s SIU. You have built working relationships with key stakeholders across Clover's clinical, compliance, claims, payment integrity, revenue operations, and legal teams, and you have begun working through your initial portfolio of fraud investigations and ad hoc referrals. By 6 months , you are independently managing a steady caseload of fraud investigations with consistently high-quality work product, in collaboration with SIU. You have a clear working rhythm with Legal and SIU, and you have built at least one working tool — a script, a notebook, a dashboard, a prompt. By 12 months , you have a track record of strong investigations, successful recoveries and/or referrals, and effective cross-functional collaboration. Senior leaders across Clover view you as a trusted person to call when they have a hunch that something doesn't look right and want it examined. You should get in touch if: Knowledge of healthcare fraud schemes & investigative experience: You have experience in healthcare fraud investigations, program integrity, or SIU operations, ideally within Medicare Advantage or managed care. You understand healthcare fraud schemes and know how to use claims data, medical records, and provider documentation to build a defensible factual record. You are AI-native and enjoy building things using LLMs: You can use LLMs to write SQL, Python, etc., to interrogate large claims and/or medical record datasets, automate investigative work, and prototype your own solutions rather than waiting for someone else to build them. We do not expect production-grade engineering or require formal technical training—we value demonstrated ability to build, ship, and showcase solutions that work. Strong communication skills: You are a strong writer and communicator who can turn complex investigative findings into clear memos, referrals, and executive summaries, and you are comfortable building in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment. Bonus points if: You have built something people actually use—an internal tool, detection model, script, automation, or AI workflow that made a manual process better. We would rather see something scrappy and useful in production than something polished in a slide. You have hands-on experience applying AI/ML to fraud, investigations, or compliance. You have a J.D., legal training, or experience working alongside Legal, SIU, or compliance at a health plan. You have industry certifications such as CFE, AHFI, or CHC. At Clover, the Business Enablement team leads our technological advancement while ensuring robust security and compliance. We deliver user-friendly corporate applications, manage complex data ecosystems, and provide efficient tech solutions across the organization. Our goal is simple: we make it easy for the business to do what’s right for Clover. We’re hiring a Engineering Lead to build the systems that help our clinical teams deliver services in the field and in members’ homes. You will own technical direction and delivery for scheduling, dispatch, field and mobile workflows, and the software that connects equipment and home technology to the operation. A likely first assignment is an “Air Traffic Control” system for field operations. A supervisor needs to understand what is happening and act when the plan breaks: a flat tire, a delayed visit, a missing piece of equipment, or a member whose availability changes. You will work with the people doing the job to decide what they need to see, what the system can help resolve, and when a human should intervene. This is a hands-on role that spans product and engineering. You will understand the business problem, shape the solution, build useful increments, and see whether they work. You may start without direct reports and can expect to coach and eventually manage one or two engineers. You should enjoy building personally and helping others become more capable. We value a tinkering instinct: try the unfamiliar tool, inspect the data, trace the failure, put a small improvement in front of a user, and learn from what happens. Hardware or connected-device experience can be a strong signal of that mindset, but it is not required. The central work is building dependable software for an operation that changes throughout the day. As an Engineering Lead, Clinical Operations, you will: Work directly with supervisors, clinical field staff, and operations leaders to understand schedules, travel, capacity, handoffs, and the exceptions that disrupt a day’s work. Build field visibility and intervention tools that give supervisors useful context, distinguish current facts from missing information, and help them respond to changing conditions. Develop scheduling and dispatch capabilities that match people and visits to practical constraints, with clear ways for operating staff to review and adjust the plan. Build and debug APIs, mobile workflows, integrations, and data flows supporting field teams, connected equipment, and home technology. Prototype quickly and ship focused increments. Make deliberate choices about what to build, integrate, or buy, and avoid committing to a large system before the operation has tested the approach. Use AI actively for development, investigation, prototypes, analysis, and useful workflow capabilities. Check the behavior and make failures understandable and recoverable. Coach engineers and take on a small number of direct reports as the team develops. Maintain clear ownership, sound engineering practices, and credible delivery commitments. Partner with Product, Special Project Leads, IT, Counterpart, and the Engagement lead at the interfaces their work shares with field operations. Success in this role looks like: First 90 days: You understand how the field operation works, have shipped an improvement used by supervisors or field staff, and can show what it changed. You have a focused technical plan grounded in real constraints and exceptions. First six months: Several useful increments are in place. Supervisors can understand and respond to disruptions more effectively, scheduling and field workflows are improving, and technical ownership is clear. You should get in touch if: You are a strong production software engineer who has owned meaningful work end-to-end and still builds regularly. You can move across backend services, APIs, data flows, user interfaces, and operational workflows to solve a real problem. You have strong product instincts, learn unfamiliar domains directly, and enjoy working with the people using what you build. You have an iterative, curious approach to technology. You can describe an unfamiliar system you explored, a practical prototype you tried, or a failure you traced across boundaries. You use AI in your own engineering work and have practical experience building or integrating AI-backed capabilities, with clear verification and evaluation. You can coach engineers and are interested in responsibility for a small team as it develops. Formal management experience can help, but a strong record of Engineering Leadership and coaching also matters. ABOUT THE JOB The ACLU seeks applicants for a full-time two-year fellowship position in the Speech, Privacy and Technology Project of the ACLU’s National office in New York, NY. The Speech, Privacy, and Technology Project is dedicated to protecting and expanding the First Amendment freedoms of expression, association, and inquiry; expanding the right to privacy and increasing the control that individuals have over their personal information; and ensuring that civil liberties are enhanced rather than compromised by new advances in science and technology. The project is currently litigating cases and conducting other advocacy efforts on a variety of issues, including political protest, freedom of expression online, privacy of electronic information, journalists’ rights, scientific and academic freedom, the free speech rights of noncitizens, openness in the courts, privacy rights at the border, and the impact of big data and algorithmic decision-making. The Brennan Fellowship, established by a special gift from author Tom Peters and poet Catherine Abbe and named after retired Supreme Court Justice William Brennan, was created to give people just starting their careers an opportunity to receive training and experience in First Amendment advocacy, and to help the ACLU advance its First Amendment goals. The Brennan Fellow will function as an integral part of the Speech, Privacy, and Technology Project, and will work on our extensive docket of First and Fourth Amendment cases. This is a two-year fellowship position, and starts in Fall 2027. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, but priority consideration will be given to applications submitted by October 1, 2026. RESPONSIBILITIES The Brennan Fellow's responsibilities will include, but will not be limited to, the following: Participating in litigation at all levels of federal and state courts, including conducting legal and factual research, interviewing clients, drafting briefs and pleadings, and assisting in discovery and motion practice Assisting in drafting amicus curiae briefs Providing support for ACLU affiliate litigation Serving as a resource for ACLU legislative and policy work Advancing ACLU policy goals through public education and through organizing and participating in coalitions Helping manage summer legal internship program and supervising student interns Engaging in special projects and other duties as assigned MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS J.D. Manage or lead projects or tasks, with assumption of greater responsibility over time. Extensive experience designing and delivering virtual and onsite professional development and coaching to local educators in Tennessee. Experience using evidence-based instructional practices and effective strategies to design and deliver professional development and adult learning. Extensive experience providing direct special education-related training, coaching, or technical assistance to local educators or instructional leaders. Familiarity with strategies to support students from a variety of cultural, linguistic, and educational backgrounds. Strong commitment to improving instructional quality and student outcomes through the use of research-based practices. Excellent interpersonal and communication skills for working with stakeholders at various levels and from a range of backgrounds. Effective communication skills with the ability to problem solve with clients and collaborate efficiently in a virtual and in-person work environment. For more than 50 years, Urban has delivered evidence and solutions that drive meaningful change, and this remains our charge today. Build a sustainable pipeline of philanthropy- and partner-supported initiatives in collaboration with Urban's leadership and development teams. https://rand.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com/en-US: Job Type: Term (Fixed Term) Position Description The RAND Corporation is a nonprofit institution that helps improve policy and decision-making through research and analysis. RAND is widely respected for operating independently of political and commercial pressures as a nonpartisan organization. RAND values objectivity and integrity in both its research processes and internal interactions and emphasizes a collegial environment that respects the contributions and dignity of all staff. RAND is seeking a Senior Researcher to lead its effort to integrate AI into RAND's research and into the business processes that support it. This is a one-year term position, renewable. The role helps set the direction for AI adoption across RAND: understanding where RAND is today, learning from peer organizations, defining what RAND needs to be good at in an AI world, and working with researchers and leadership to make adoption real at scale. The position is well suited to someone who has used AI directly in research and business work, has helped other organizations build AI into their core functions, and can move a large, expert community toward practical use. Key Responsibilities External learning: Draw lessons from peer organizations, including FFRDCs, UARCs, and consulting firms, on what distinguishes successful adoption from failed attempts, and translate them to RAND's context. Strategic direction: Recommend a framework for how AI fits across RAND's diverse portfolio. Adoption at scale: Design and test approaches with researchers on real projects, including quick wins that build momentum, and define what AI tools need to look like to be used well inside RAND's culture and research practice. Tools and resources: Advise on the tool landscape (what to keep, build, buy, or stop), how separate tool efforts should work together, and how to allocate resources, with attention to security, compliance, and budget constraints. Governance and measurement: Propose how decisions about AI deployment should be made and define evidence-based measures of whether adoption is working. Qualifications All research positions at RAND require excellent analytic skills; the ability to communicate clearly and effectively in English, both orally and in writing; the ability to work effectively as a member of a multi-disciplinary team; and a strong commitment to RAND's core values of quality and objectivity. Required: Experience integrating AI to transform research and business processes. Demonstrated ability to lead a cross-organizational effort, working with senior leaders and with technical and non-technical staff. Ability to synthesize evidence from interviews, usage data, and external practice into clear recommendations for leadership. Experience moving users from skepticism to routine use of new tools. Familiarity with research organizations, FFRDCs, or similar institutions. Preferred: Experience with AI governance, security, and compliance requirements. Education Requirements and Experience The preferred candidate will have a PhD and 8+ years of experience, or a Master's degree with thesis and 13+ years of experience, in computer science or engineering, information science, cyber engineering, or related field (such as mathematics, operations research, physical sciences, or closely related discipline). Professional experience should demonstrate the applicant’s ability to design, execute and disseminate results of research using analytically rigorous methods. Location Fully remote Salary Range : $171,800 - $283,100 RAND considers a variety of factors when formulating an offer, including but not limited to, the specific role and associated responsibilities; a candidate's work experience, education/training, skills, expertise; and internal equity. This position is eligible for overtime. The salary range includes base pay plus RAND's sabbatic pay (which provides additional compensation above base pay when vacation is taken). Job Type: Regular Physical Security Analyst Overview The Physical Security Analyst plays an important role in protecting RAND’s people, facilities, assets, and classified information. This individual contributor supports the day-to-day delivery of a comprehensive physical security program across unclassified spaces, closed areas, and Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities (SCIFs). Partnering closely with the Physical Security Manager, the Physical Security Analyst helps maintain a secure, compliant, and service-oriented environment. Responsibilities include assessing physical security risks, supporting access-control and security-system operations, coordinating with the contract guard force, and identifying practical improvements to policies, procedures, and facility safeguards. The ideal candidate brings sound judgment, technical aptitude, attention to detail, and a collaborative approach to resolving security issues in a dynamic environment. This position requires 100% in-office support and may require occasional after-hours support. Duties and Responsibilities Evaluate and maintain compliance with the National Industrial Security Program Operating Manual (NISPOM), 32 CFR Part 117, ICD 705, applicable NIST 800-171 physical security requirements, Security Technical Implementation Guides (STIGs), and other applicable requirements. Conduct physical security risk assessments to identify facility vulnerabilities, evaluate potential risks, and recommend and implement mitigation strategies. Prepare and review security documentation, fixed-facility checklists, and standard operating procedures (SOPs) to support government audits, inspections, and assessments. Analyze physical security metrics and recommend improvements to operational effectiveness and compliance. Oversee access control for open (unclassified), closed (classified), and SCIF areas. Operate and administer the Access Control System (ACS) database, ensuring accuracy and compliance with established security procedures. Enroll personnel into security systems and issue corporate and government-mandated identification badges. Verify security clearances and access authorizations for employees, contractors, and visitors; resolve access-related discrepancies. Evaluate access-control procedures and recommend improvements to strengthen facility security. Monitor and program facility Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) and Closed-Circuit Television (CCTV) networks; identify and address security-system deficiencies. Coordinate preventive maintenance and emergency repairs for alarms, cameras, electronic locks, and related security equipment. Troubleshoot complex security-system hardware and software issues in coordination with external integration vendors. Review and analyze system logs and archived video footage to investigate security incidents or anomalies and recommend corrective actions. Assist with coordinating assignments and operational needs for the contract security guard force. Support company events to help ensure the security and safety of facilities and visitors. Perform other related duties as assigned. Basic Qualifications Strong knowledge of ICD 705 Technical Specifications, 32 CFR Part 117, and physical security requirements applicable to classified facilities and SCIFs. Knowledge of access-control systems, intrusion detection systems, and CCTV systems. Experience supporting physical security operations in unclassified, classified, and/or SCIF environments. Experience administering access-control databases and verifying personnel clearances and access authorizations. Knowledge of Communications Security (COMSEC) requirements and procedures. Ability to independently evaluate security risks, recommend corrective actions, and troubleshoot complex technical problems. Experience coordinating assignments for contract security guards. Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills, with close attention to detail. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Proficiency with Microsoft Office applications and relevant security tools. Ability to prepare security documentation, SOPs, checklists, reports, and audit materials. Must be able to pass a background check. Education Bachelor’s degree in Security Management, Criminal Justice, or a related field required. An equivalent combination of education and relevant work experience may be considered in lieu of a bachelor’s degree. Experience Bachelor’s degree: At least five years of relevant experience in physical security operations, access-control systems, classified facility security, security systems administration, or a related security discipline required. Without a bachelor’s degree: At least nine years of relevant experience required. Security Clearance Must hold and maintain an active Top Secret security clearance and be able to obtain and maintain SCI eligibility. Travel Up to 15% travel between RAND offices Location This position will be located in RAND’s Washington, DC, office and requires a presence of five days per week, Monday through Friday, generally from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. This position requires 100% onsite work; remote and hybrid work arrangements are not available. Occasional after-hours support may be required. Salary Range : $88,000 - $130,900 RAND considers a variety of factors when formulating an offer, including but not limited to, the specific role and associated responsibilities; a candidate’s work experience, education/training, skills, expertise; and internal equity. The salary range includes base pay plus RAND’s sabbatic pay (which provides additional compensation above base pay when vacation is taken). In addition, RAND provides strong benefits including health insurance coverage, life and disability insurance, savings plan, paid time-off and more. Equal Opportunity Employer

https://jobs.tufts.edu/jobs/23787?lang=e: Overview The Allen Discovery Center is dedicated to the advancement of basic biology and biomedicine, and to becoming a leader in an integrated approach to the control of biological structure and function. Exploiting novel mechanisms of cellular decision-making, we seek to understand and augment the information processing, computation, and patterning processes that implement the generation and regenerative repair of anatomical structures. Examples of such tools include AI applied to design and construction, digital twins, reality capture and drones, sensing and structural health monitoring, data analytics, and construction robotics. Candidates are not expected to have expertise in all of these areas; we welcome applicants whose strength lies in one or two of them, paired with a solid grounding in civil, architectural, or construction engineering practice. This is a career-track teaching appointment with a clear path for promotion to Associate Teaching Professor and Teaching Professor. Teaching faculty at WPI are full voting members of the faculty and play a central role in curricular leadership. JOB DESCRIPTION Responsibilities Teach undergraduate and graduate courses in civil infrastructure and the built environment, integrating digital, sensing, and automation technologies into instruction. Develop new courses or laboratory modules that give students hands-on experience with modern field, sensing, and computational tools. Advise and mentor students in WPI’s project-based curriculum, including Major Qualifying Projects (MQP), Interactive Qualifying Projects (IQP), and graduate capstone work. Help shape laboratory, maker, and field-testing facilities that support instruction in construction and infrastructure technology. Build relationships with contractors, owners, agencies, and technology firms so that instruction reflects current practice. Participate in departmental service, student recruiting and retention, curriculum assessment and ABET accreditation activities, and outreach. Required Qualifications An earned doctorate by the appointment start date in civil engineering, architectural engineering, construction engineering, or a closely related field. Expertise in one or more digital, sensing, or automation technologies relevant to civil infrastructure, with a grounding in civil, architectural, or construction engineering and the ability to connect these technologies to construction processes, structural behavior, or infrastructure performance. Enthusiasm for hands-on, project-based, and experiential instruction. Preferred Qualifications Prior university-level teaching experience, including course or laboratory development. Professional experience in the construction industry, with an infrastructure owner or agency, or in a construction or infrastructure technology firm. Experience with industry partnerships, sponsored student projects, or workforce development programs. A record of mentoring students from a range of backgrounds and preparing them to work on diverse teams. About the Department and WPI WPI is a global leader in project-based learning. Its distinctive undergraduate curriculum requires every student to complete substantial team-based projects addressing real problems for real stakeholders, often at one of WPI’s project centers around the world. Undergraduate courses are delivered in an intensive seven-week term structure that supports focused, immersive instruction. CEAE offers ABET-accredited undergraduate programs and graduate degrees spanning civil engineering, construction project management, environmental engineering, and architectural engineering. The department is investing in the technologies that will define the next generation of infrastructure practice, and this position is central to that direction. The successful candidate will find natural collaborators across WPI in robotics engineering, data science, electrical and computer engineering, and computer science. Worcester, Massachusetts is New England’s second-largest city, with a growing innovation economy, a substantial construction and real estate development sector, and easy access to Boston, Providence, and Hartford. How to Apply Applications should be submitted through WPI’s online application system and include: A cover letter describing the candidate’s interest in and fit for the position. A curriculum vitae. A statement of teaching philosophy and interests (2 pages maximum), including courses the candidate would be prepared to teach and any new courses or laboratory experiences they would propose to develop. Names and contact information for three professional references. References will not be contacted without the candidate’s permission. Review of applications will begin February 1, 2027, and will continue until the position is filled. Inquiries may be directed to Prof. Nima Rahbar at nrahbar@wpi.edu. JOB TITLE Institutional Research Analyst LOCATION Worcester DEPARTMENT NAME Institutional Research, Analytics & Assessment DIVISION NAME Worcester Polytechnic Institute - WPI JOB DESCRIPTION SUMMARY The Institutional Research Analyst supports data-informed decision-making through dashboard development, institutional analysis, and higher education market research. The position transforms data from multiple sources into reliable, accessible, and actionable insights to support institutional planning, assessment, enrollment strategies, and academic program development. The Analyst develops and maintains analytical products, interprets institutional and market data, and communicates findings through clear visualizations, reports, and presentations. Working collaboratively with campus stakeholders, the Analyst helps improve data quality, accessibility, and data literacy to inform institutional planning and decision-making. The Analyst is part of a dynamic, collaborative team that values curiosity, continuous improvement, and shared problem-solving. The ideal candidate is comfortable navigating ambiguity, balancing competing priorities, and developing practical solutions to evolving analytical needs. JOB DESCRIPTION 1. Dashboard Development, Data Visualization, and Data Management Develop and maintain interactive dashboards, visualizations, and reporting tools that support institutional planning, assessment, and decision-making. Prepare, integrate, and validate data from multiple sources, improving accuracy, reliability, and efficiency through repeatable and automated processes. Translate stakeholder needs into effective reporting solutions and document data sources, definitions, and processes to support consistent interpretation and data quality. 2. Institutional Analysis and Market Research Conduct analyses of institutional data related to students, enrollment, academic programs, research, institutional effectiveness, and strategic priorities. Research higher education trends, peer institutions, demographics, academic programs, and market conditions to identify opportunities and inform enrollment strategies and institutional planning. Communicate findings through clear reports, presentations, and other analytical products that support decision-making by university leadership and campus stakeholders. 3. Collaboration, Process Improvement, and Data Literacy Collaborate with academic departments and administrative teams on analytical projects and initiatives that improve access to and effective use of institutional information. Identify opportunities to streamline reporting processes, improve operational efficiency, and enhance data accessibility and service delivery. Develop documentation, quick-reference guides, infographics, newsletters, and training materials that promote data literacy and awareness of institutional research resources. Other duties may be assigned. Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree in a relevant field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience. At least one year of relevant experience in institutional research, data analytics, business intelligence, higher education research, or a related area. Experience preparing, cleaning, validating, and analyzing data from multiple sources and developing dashboards, reports, or data visualizations. Strong analytical, critical-thinking, and problem-solving skills, including the ability to identify data issues, interpret findings, and work through ambiguous or open-ended questions. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex information to nontechnical audiences. Strong attention to detail and data quality, along with the ability to manage multiple assignments, meet deadlines, and work independently and collaboratively. Preferred Qualifications Master's degree in higher education, social science, data analytics, statistics, public policy, business, or a related field. Experience working in institutional research or higher education. Experience with Power BI or a comparable data visualization platform, including data modeling, DAX, Power Query, or automated data preparation. Experience with R, Python, SPSS, or comparable statistical or programming software.
