JOB TITLE Director, Systems Engineering LOCATION Worcester DEPARTMENT NAME Infrastructure Services and Architecture DIVISION NAME Worcester Polytechnic Institute - WPI JOB DESCRIPTION SUMMARY Reporting to the Assistant Chief Technology Officer, Infrastructure Services and Architecture, the Director of Systems Engineering will lead the team responsible for the university's servers, storage, cloud computing, and virtualization, along with infrastructure DevOps, application system and security support, and the technology behind Campus Safety Services (card access, video surveillance, emergency radios, and emergency phones). WPI's information technology environment is highly distributed and diverse. This senior leadership role combines strategic vision and planning with direct, hands-on technical involvement alongside the engineers who report to the role. The Director is responsible for the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the systems that support the university's educational and operational objectives, and for the reliability of the systems that support campus safety. This position is hybrid, with 4 days on campus in Worcester and 1 day from home. JOB DESCRIPTION Strategic Leadership and Team Development Develop and implement a comprehensive systems strategy aligned with the university's goals and objectives. Collaborate with the Assistant CTO and other senior leaders to prioritize systems initiatives and align them with institutional priorities. Develop staff, set clear performance expectations, and manage workload and operational tasks across the systems team. Work with other groups within IT and other business units to develop solutions for unique system requirements, including technical and regulatory requirements. Systems, Storage, Virtualization, and Cloud Engineering Working directly with the Systems Engineers who report to this role, direct the design, implementation, and management of the university's physical and virtual server infrastructure, enterprise storage and backup platforms, and AWS and Azure cloud environments. Participate actively in solution design, technical review, and implementation planning alongside the engineering team. Ensure efficient use of resources through effective virtualization, capacity planning, and lifecycle management. Lead the evaluation, selection, and adoption of new platform technologies. Ensure new implementations are documented, supportable, and aligned with institutional standards and architecture. Systems Operations and Administration Oversee the team that performs the day-to-day operation and administration of the university's systems environment, ensuring stability, availability, and performance. Ensure all key services, systems, and components are under appropriate monitoring and alerting. Ensure operating system patching, firmware maintenance, and lifecycle activities are performed on a defined and predictable cadence. Ensure documentation, asset inventory, and configuration records are up to date and accurate. Serve as the senior escalation point during major incidents, directing the response, restoring service, and driving root cause analysis and preventive action to completion. Ensure systems incidents and service requests are resolved within the applicable SLA, maintaining open communication with other ITS teams, including the Service Desk. DevOps, Automation, and Process Improvement Manage the DevOps resource supporting the infrastructure organization, directing the work against strategic DevOps and automation requirements from the Assistant CTO. Identify repeated work and recurring requests across all areas reporting to this role. Define, document, and standardize the processes behind that work so it can be measured and performed consistently by both full-time employees and the managed service provider. Identify and prioritize the automation opportunities with the greatest return on team efficiency, and direct their design, build, and adoption. Measure the effect of automation and process improvement on toil, cycle time, and error rates, and adjust priorities based on results. Application System and Security Support Own the systems and middleware layer beneath the university's enterprise and departmental applications, including database platforms, web services, and load balancing. Ensure these platforms are appropriately sized, patched, monitored, hardened, and recoverable. Partner with application owners and the Office of Information Security to remediate vulnerabilities and apply security controls at the system and middleware layer. Coordinate maintenance windows and upgrade planning with application stakeholders to minimize disruption to academic and administrative operations. Campus Safety Services Oversee the technology, operation, and support of campus safety systems, including physical card access, video surveillance, emergency radios, and the emergency phone system. Ensure the security, reliability, and availability of these physical security and life-safety systems. Oversee deployment, upgrade, and lifecycle planning for campus safety technology, including coverage associated with building renovation and construction projects. Collaborate with Campus Police, Facilities, and external vendors and integrators to align technology capability with campus safety requirements. Security, Compliance, and Resilience Ensure all systems components meet institutional security and compliance requirements, applying best practices across all infrastructure reporting to this role. Ensure system designs and procedures are aligned with, and capable of enforcing, university policies and best practices. Ensure backup, recovery, and business continuity capabilities are designed, documented, and regularly tested against defined recovery objectives. Ensure vulnerabilities are remediated within institutional service level targets, and provide the Information Security operations team with the access and tooling needed to identify, locate, and isolate systems involved in security incidents. Support audit activity and the production of control evidence, and assist Information Security in drafting policies that overlap with the systems team. Budget, Vendor, and Resource Management Develop and manage the operating and capital budget for the systems team and campus safety technology. Identify opportunities for cost savings and license optimization. Oversee vendor relationships and negotiate contracts for systems, storage, cloud, and campus safety services and products, working directly with vendors, resellers, and integrators. Plan and forecast refresh and renewal cycles to support multi-year budget development. Performs all other duties and responsibilities as assigned or directed by the supervisor. QUALIFICATIONS Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Information Systems, Information Technology, or a related field, or equivalent experience. Minimum of 7 years of experience, including direct leadership of a systems, infrastructure, or operations team. Strong leadership and team management skills, with the ability to develop and retain technical staff. Excellent strategic thinking and planning abilities. Deep, hands-on understanding of server, storage, virtualization, and cloud computing technologies across both Windows and Linux environments. Working knowledge of the middleware layer supporting enterprise applications, including database platforms, web services, and load balancing. Experience directing DevOps and automation work. Knowledge of physical access control, video surveillance, and emergency communications systems. Strong problem-solving and decision-making capabilities, including the ability to serve as a senior escalation point during major incidents. Excellent communication and interpersonal skills. Experience developing and managing operating and capital budgets and negotiating with vendors. PREFERRED CERTIFICATIONS Certifications are preferred, not required, and no candidate

JOB TITLE Practice Point Technical Operations Manager LOCATION Worcester DEPARTMENT NAME Biomanufacturing Education and Training Center - BETC DIVISION NAME Worcester Polytechnic Institute - WPI JOB DESCRIPTION SUMMARY The Technical Operations Manager (TFM) of PracticePoint is responsible for the proper functioning of all aspects of the facility and for technical innovation, enabling the fulfillment of its mission of supporting research and development across the breadth of medical technology. The TFM will also serve as the Director of the Medical Engineering and Imaging Core (MEIC), a core facility that supports WPI faculty and students in efficiently using the equipment in PracticePoint. The TFM will work closely with the PracticePoint Director and staff to ensure that the facilities are equipped and operating for sustainable success, with appropriate plans for maintenance and upgrades. The TFM will participate, as appropriate, in the research and development work carried out in the facility as well as in outreach and identification of new members and facility users. The TFM must be qualified, or become qualified, to operate the MRI machine, fluoroscope, surgical lasers, and other sophisticated and potentially hazardous equipment. The TFM is responsible for the overall safe operation of the facility. JOB DESCRIPTION Responsibilities: Manage MEIC operations. Work with faculty and students on facility use scheduling, technical support, financial arrangements (billing and invoicing), and facility equipment maintenance. Research potential members, conduct technically oriented facility tours, and plan clients' use of the facilities. Work with members, potential members, and other users to obtain maximum effectiveness from use of the facilities. This requires in-depth knowledge of the capabilities of the equipment as well as knowledge of the healthcare areas being studied. Participate in PracticePoint dry and wet lab events, including pre-lab setup and preparation, intra-lab support, and post-lab cleaning and follow-up. Work with the Director of PracticePoint, PracticePoint staff, and PracticePoint-affiliated faculty to conduct research on novel medical technologies in robotics, AI, imaging, and materials. Maintain oversight of the facilities with regard to maintenance and upgrades so that the facility continues to meet the needs of WPI researchers and external members. Obtain and maintain appropriate training credentials and approvals for operation of all PracticePoint equipment, including the MRI, fluoroscope, lasers, and machine shops, together with appropriate credentials for training other users and operators. Oversee the delivery and use of all hazardous materials, and maintain currency with safety standards and regulatory requirements for all aspects of the facility. Maintain close coordination with the Environmental Health and Safety Office as well as relevant committees, including the IRB, IBC, and IACUC. Have and oversee access to all areas of the facility, based on either card or physical key access. Oversee, with the Business Manager, facility scheduling and charge rates for internal and external users. Performs all other duties and responsibilities as assigned or directed by the supervisor. Qualifications: Master's or PhD degree in Biomedical or Medical Robotics Engineering or a closely related area such as Biophysics or Life Science required. PhD preferred. Two or more years of hands-on experience with medical imaging equipment operations (MRI, C-arm, ultrasound, etc.). Previous research experience in Biomedical or Medical Robotics areas preferred. Excellent knowledge of MS Office, databases, and information systems. Excellent written and oral communication skills. Ability to work independently to accomplish the position requirements, while also being effective as part of the PracticePoint team. Strong creativity and problem-solving skills. Demonstrated experience in planning and plan execution. Job Description: The Senior Research Analyst, Prospect Development, serves as a strategic partner to fundraising teams, identifying and evaluating individuals, foundations, and corporations with the capacity and inclination to support Brown University. This role conducts in-depth research and sophisticated wealth analysis to advance institutional fundraising priorities. Key responsibilities include preparing high-level briefing materials for leadership and senior administrators; evaluating business affiliations and networks to inform prospect qualification and strategy; and delivering analytical insights that guide the cultivation of principal, major, and leadership-level donors. The Senior Research Analyst interprets complex wealth indicators—including equity holdings, executive compensation, and complex asset structures—and translates findings into clear, actionable recommendations. The role also conducts highly sensitive due diligence research on prospective and current donors, assessing potential reputational, financial, and legal risks. Using advanced research methodologies and AI-enabled tools, the Senior Research Analyst ensures accuracy while upholding the highest standards of confidentiality and data governance. Success in this role requires sound judgment, discretion, and the ability to synthesize complex financial, professional, and biographical information into concise, strategic insights. The ideal candidate brings exceptional attention to detail, strong written and verbal communication skills, intellectual curiosity, and adaptability in a rapidly evolving technological landscape, along with a demonstrated ability to prioritize a dynamic workload, respond to evolving needs, and exercise sound judgment in time-sensitive situations. Education and Experience Bachelor’s degree or equivalent combination of education and experience. Minimum of 4 years of experience in advanced research, development, fundraising, and/or market research experience. Job Competencies Demonstrated expertise in research and analytical methods, including the ability to gather, evaluate, and synthesize complex information from multiple sources and translate findings into clear, actionable insights. Advanced written communication and editing skills, with the ability to produce concise, accurate materials under tight deadlines and distill complex financial and biographical information for diverse audiences. Strong digital and technical proficiency, including advanced online search strategies, complex database use, and familiarity with research tools such as iWave, LexisNexis, Candid, and Xapien. As well as a high level of computer proficiency with advanced working knowledge of the Windows/Google Workspace environment. Ability to work independently with initiative and accountability while contributing effectively in a collaborative team environment, demonstrating sound judgment and strong working relationships. Proven ability to manage multiple projects and competing priorities, solve problems effectively, and meet demanding deadlines in a fast-paced environment. Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to engage professionally with a wide range of stakeholders, demonstrating tact, diplomacy, and adaptability. High degree of professionalism, ethical awareness, and discretion, with the ability to manage confidential information and apply sound judgment. Commitment to fostering an inclusive environment, with the ability to work respectfully across varied perspectives. Strong financial analysis and information retrieval skills, including the ability to assess wealth indicators and philanthropic capacity among high-net-worth populations. Preferred Qualifications Preference given to candidates with an understanding of the prospect research competencies presented in the Association of Professional Researchers for Advancement (APRA) Body of Knowledge Experience in nonprofit, higher education, or research environments, particularly in fundraising or development, is preferred. https://thejacksonlaboratory.wd503.mywor: We are seeking an exceptional Lead Scientist to join our Rare Disease Research team in a senior, high-impact role. This position is central to our mission of advancing the understanding and treatment of epilepsy, and is suited to an accomplished researcher who combines deep mechanistic expertise with a strong drive toward therapeutic translation. The Lead Scientist will spearhead electrophysiology-based research programs using both in vivo mouse models and ex vivo brain slice preparations, generate and own key datasets, mentor junior scientists, and contribute meaningfully to our drug and therapeutic pipeline. This role offers significant scientific autonomy and the opportunity to shape the direction of the epilepsy program. In Vivo Research & Mouse Models Design, execute, and lead seizure studies using established and novel mouse models of epilepsy (e.g., kainate, pilocarpine, kindling, genetic models such as Scn1a+/−). Plan and perform chronic in vivo electrophysiological recordings (EEG/LFP) to quantify seizure burden, inter-ictal activity, and network dynamics. Oversee surgical implantation of recording electrodes and manage long-term telemetric monitoring cohorts. Develop and validate new in vivo model systems relevant to drug-resistant or pediatric epilepsies. Ex Vivo Electrophysiology Execute and lead acute and organotypic brain slice preparation with high reproducibility across hippocampal, cortical, and thalamocortical circuits. Perform whole-cell patch-clamp and field potential recordings to characterize intrinsic neuronal excitability, synaptic transmission, and network-level epileptiform activity. Analyze pharmacological modulation of ion channels, GABAergic/glutamatergic systems, and other therapeutic targets in slice preparations. Therapeutic Development Serve as the primary electrophysiology lead in evaluating candidate therapeutics (small molecules, biologics, gene therapy approaches) across preclinical models. Design and execute dose-response, time-course, and mechanistic studies to characterize compound efficacy and tolerability in the CNS. Partner closely with medicinal chemistry, pharmacology, and translational teams to align preclinical findings with clinical hypotheses. Contribute to IND-enabling studies and regulatory submissions by providing high-quality preclinical data packages. Scientific Leadership & Collaboration Lead a small team of research scientists and associates, providing mentorship, experimental guidance, and career development support. Define research priorities, drive experimental strategy, and ensure rigorous, reproducible science across the team. Present findings at internal research reviews, external conferences, and in peer-reviewed publications. Build and maintain collaborations with academic KOLs, clinical epileptologists, and external research partners. Contribute to grant writing, scientific communications, and IP generation as appropriate. Required Qualifications PhD in Neuroscience, Pharmacology, Physiology, or a closely related discipline. Minimum 8 years of post-doctoral research experience, with a demonstrated track record in epilepsy or seizure biology. Expert-level proficiency in in vivo electrophysiology, including EEG recording and analysis in rodent seizure models. Expert-level proficiency in brain slice preparation and patch-clamp or field potential electrophysiology. Extensive hands-on experience with rodent models of epilepsy and associated surgical, behavioral, and data analysis workflows. Direct experience contributing to preclinical therapeutic development programs, including target validation and compound profiling. Strong publication record in peer-reviewed journals relevant to epilepsy, ion channel biology, or CNS pharmacology. Demonstrated ability to independently design, execute, and interpret complex experiments and communicate findings clearly. Preferred Qualifications Experience with genetic mouse models of epilepsy (e.g., Dravet syndrome, KCNQ2, CDKL5). Familiarity with advanced imaging modalities (e.g., calcium imaging, optogenetics) in the context of seizure research. Experience with translational biomarker development or clinical EEG interpretation. Prior experience in a biotech, pharma, or translational research environment. Familiarity with regulatory expectations for preclinical CNS packages (FDA/EMA guidelines). Experience with gene therapy or RNA-based therapeutic modalities. Skills & Competencies Scientific rigor and meticulous attention to reproducibility and data quality. Strong analytical and quantitative skills; proficiency with electrophysiology analysis software (e.g., Clampfit, Spike2, custom MATLAB/Python pipelines). Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present complex data to cross-functional stakeholders. Collaborative mindset with the ability to work effectively across disciplines and organizational boundaries. Self-motivated, proactive, and capable of managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced research environment. Demonstrated leadership ability, including mentoring junior scientists and driving team-level deliverables. What We Offer A senior, high-visibility role at the forefront of epilepsy research and drug discovery. Significant scientific autonomy and the opportunity to shape the direction of a core research program. A collaborative, mission-driven culture with access to state-of-the-art research infrastructure. Competitive compensation package including base salary, bonus, and equity. Comprehensive benefits including medical, dental, vision, and generous PTO. Support for conference attendance, publications, and continued professional development. Proficiency in experimental design, data analysis, and interpretation. Excellent leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills. The Knowledge Systems Group (KSG) builds systems for precision oncology at Dana-Farber, including MatchMiner for clinical trial matching and the cBioPortal for exploration of cancer clinico-genomic data. These systems draw on standard analytical outputs as well as supplemental genomic, transcriptomic and clinical biomarkers generated by KSG. This role focuses on generating those supplemental biomarkers, contributing the genomics, transcriptomics and bioinformatics expertise to support it. In this role, you will work with DFCI faculty to understand their requests and translate those into clear specifications that the engineering team can build. The Scientist II works directly with oncologists, pathologists, and researchers to prioritize biomarker selection, establish requirements, select computational methods, develop quality control metrics, prototype data visualization and delivery mechanisms, and transform these scientific decisions into technical specifications which engineers can readily implement. Much of the current work centers on genomic and transcriptomic profiling data: targeted cancer gene panel, whole exome DNA (WES), and RNA sequencing. Those data get turned into clinical biomarkers for trial matching and captured in cBioPortal for research exploration. This is a multi-omics literate role that faces outward. The Scientist II has to be fluent enough in cancer genomics and transcriptomics to earn a researcher's trust, and comfortable enough with software to keep several concurrent builds organized and on track. The Fischer Lab at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute is a Structural and Chemical Biology lab that combines molecular biology, computational biology, structural biology and chemistry with various ‘Omics’ techniques such as proteomics to study the pathways and protein complexes involved in protein homeostasis and the ubiquitin proteasome system often associated with human diseases, including cancer. The Fischer lab integrates structural biology, molecular biology and computational guided approaches to address fundamental questions about the mechanistic principles that govern signaling through the ubiquitin proteasome system. The Fischer Lab (https://fischerlab.org/) seeks a highly motivated individual to join the research team as a Cryo-EM SCIENTIST who will work on various structural biology and biochemical projects addressing fundamental questions in our understanding of the ubiquitin system and ways we can manipulate this system with molecular glues and degrader molecules for therapeutic purposes. In addition, you will assist with training and mentoring Fischer lab members in sample preparation for both cryoEM and negative stain EM and data processing for various projects. While we consider various backgrounds, practical experience with cryo-EM and a strong interest in understanding how molecular machines work and the desire to tackle a major problem of great significance are absolutely essential. Our laboratory is based at Dana-Farber Cancer Institute in Longwood Center and is an affiliate of the BCMP department at Harvard Medical School. We are affiliated with state of the art facilities for structural biology (cryo-EM, X-ray crystallography, NMR), chemistry, biophysics, cellular imaging, etc. and the lab also has expertise and equipment for mass spectrometry including timsTOF pro/ultra and Orbitrap Eclipse/zoom mass spectrometers. Join our highly interactive team of scientists, postdocs, graduate students and technicians to work on understand signaling through the ubiquitin proteasome pathway and leverage these insights to test new avenues for therapeutic development. All nudge unit activities will further BCBSMA’s strategic pillars: quality, equity, affordability, and consumer experience. The challenge at the centre of this role is the distance between a demo and a product. A model that works in a notebook is not a feature that works for hundreds of millions of players, or a tool a game team trusts with their daily work. Help us Close that gap: the evaluation that tells you it's actually good, the latency and cost envelope that makes it viable, the failure modes you find before players do, and the plumbing that makes it boring to operate. We're not looking for someone who wants to train a frontier model. We're looking for someone who gets unreasonable results out of the ones that exist.

We are looking for someone to build and ship: AI features in live games, and the internal tools that give superpowers to Supercellians. Some of that work will take you inside a game or central team for a while, close enough to their craft to build the right thing with them.

 - Build and ship AI features and systems end to end into live games and internal tools, at production quality and under real deadlines.

 - Do the applied engineering that makes AI work in practice.

 - Fine-tune, adapt, and distill models where it pays off, and have the judgment to know when a better prompt, better retrieval, or a smaller model beats training anything.

 - Make sound trade-offs on inference, including on-device where it matters, against real parameter, latency, and battery targets, without losing the feel players expect.

 - Take on the harder applied problems, such as making autonomous agents reliable and accurate enough to trust with real work.

 - Stay at the frontier by reading the literature and following the major conferences, and bring back what is genuinely useful.


WHAT YOU HAVE

 - A track record of shipping LLM or generative AI applications that real users used, in production, not prototypes. We value this far above a publication record.

 - Real software engineering depth. You write code others can maintain, and you own things in production rather than handing them off.

 - Hands-on experience writing and maintaining benchmarks and evaluation frameworks, ideally across more than one modality.

https://job-boards.greenhouse.io/smartly: We are looking for a Senior Data Platform Engineer to join the Data Platform at Smartly! Smartly is building the standard path for governed data sharing across product services, analytics, and AI/ML. The Data Platform team owns the contracts, control mechanisms, publication paths, catalog metadata, lifecycle rules, lineage, permissions, and runtime building blocks that make reusable data safe and practical at scale. This is a role for someone who wants to shape a platform early, while working on concrete production problems from the start. Smartly already has the production systems, Kafka backbone, PostgreSQL databases, analytical consumers, and AI/ML use cases that need a better data foundation. The challenge is to turn that reality into a standard path that engineers actually want to use. Our first milestone is focused: centrally managed publishing tables in service-owned PostgreSQL databases, captured through Debezium CDC into Kafka, and registered in DataHub with ownership, lifecycle, lineage, and impact-analysis metadata. Longer-term, the platform expands toward self-service data products, governed materialisations, durable shared state, and reusable data across Smartly’s operational and analytical systems. This is not a role where you only maintain an existing reporting pipeline. You will help design and build the platform path that other engineering teams use when they publish and consume shared data. What you will do Design and build platform services, tools, and workflows for contract-driven data publishing and consumption. Build the first production path for platform-managed PostgreSQL publishing tables, Debezium CDC, Kafka topics, and catalog registration. Create GitOps-style workflows where contracts, schemas, ownership, lifecycle, compatibility, policy metadata, and runtime desired state are reviewed, validated, and reconciled as code. Build tooling that gives product engineers fast feedback before they publish or change data products. Help define how Smartly models data products, publishing contracts, schema evolution, field stability, deletion semantics, access policy, lineage, and cost attribution. Operate and improve the CDC runtime model, including Kubernetes workloads, source-specific isolation, offsets, schema history, heartbeats, signal channels, lag visibility, replay, resnapshotting, and recovery. Integrate platform metadata into DataHub so engineers can discover data products, understand ownership, trace lineage, and reason about the impact of changes. Work with product, infrastructure, data engineering, analytics, and AI/ML teams to make the standard path easier and safer than bespoke point-to-point integrations. What we are looking for Strong experience building and operating production software systems, preferably in platform, infrastructure, backend, or data-intensive environments. Deep understanding of distributed systems trade-offs: reliability, idempotency, replay, eventual consistency, ownership boundaries, compatibility, and operational failure modes. Practical experience with PostgreSQL or other relational databases, including schema design, migrations, transactions, replication, or operational performance. Experience with Kafka, event streaming, CDC, Debezium, or adjacent data-movement technologies. Direct Debezium experience is valuable, but strong fundamentals matter more. Experience building software that other engineers use: CLIs, internal platforms, control planes, automation, CI validation, developer tooling, or self-service workflows. Familiarity with Kubernetes and cloud or infrastructure platforms, including runtime isolation, deployment, observability, and operational ownership. Ability to turn ambiguous architectural direction into practical increments, make trade-offs explicit, and deliver useful production systems without waiting for perfect certainty. Clear written and spoken communication in English. This role involves aligning multiple engineering teams around standards, contracts, and ownership boundaries. Useful experience, but not required DataHub or other data catalog, lineage, or governance systems. Open table formats such as Apache Iceberg, object-store-backed data lakes, S3, BigQuery, ClickHouse, or analytical storage systems. GitHub Actions, policy-as-code, infrastructure-as-code, controllers, operators, or reconciliation-based systems. Data contracts, schema registries, Protobuf, Avro, JSON Schema, compatibility checking, field-level metadata, or contract testing. Experience supporting analytics, AI/ML, feature-store-style access patterns, or cross-domain product-service integrations. Experience with JVM languages and Python, TypeScript, Go, or Ruby. Global impact through technology used by major brands to plan, create, optimize, and understand digital advertising at scale. A flexible hybrid workplace that balances office collaboration with focused remote work. At Smartly we work 3 days a week from the office. YOUR IMPACT 

The Planning & Analysis domain empowers the organisation with accurate, granular insights and drives proactive decision making that stays aligned with our growth plans and cost envelope.

This role is fundamental in connecting long term workforce strategy to daily execution. You will translate hiring, attrition and spend signals into clear guidance for the People & Places (P&P) team, talent acquisition and the business leaders they support.

WHAT YOU'LL SHIP

 - Own how Mollie tracks, measures and forecasts headcount, including the headcount model, hiring plan, attrition and open role view, and the link between headcount and budget.

 - Lead the analytical response to our most important workforce questions, such as sizing hiring needs, stress testing plan assumptions, and building the case for new teams and locations.

 - Build and own models that break headcount and people cost down into their key drivers (hiring pace, attrition, mix, seniority, location), giving P&P and senior leaders the visibility to prioritise and act with confidence.

 - Walk P&P through the trends in people data and the story behind them, including spend and other relevant metrics such as People OPEX, Places costs and vendor spend.

 - Own the people and headcount view end to end in our monthly business reviews and in the annual planning cycle.
   
   


WHAT YOU'LL BRING

 - 3 to 5 years of experience in FP&A, workforce planning or people analytics, ideally within a high growth fintech, tech or payments company. Your academic background is in a quantitative or business field.

 - You are very comfortable using AI tooling in your daily work, and this is a must. You use it to accelerate your output, pressure test your thinking, automate recurring work and remove the grunt work that gets in the way of insight.

 - Experience with Pigment, our planning tool, or with a comparable planning platform (Anaplan, Adaptive, or similar).

 - You are action oriented by nature. Your analysis does not stop at describing what happened. You formulate a recommendation and stand behind it.

 - You handle sensitive people data with discretion and good judgement.

No matter if you're aiming for promotion, exploring a different career path or building new skills, you'll be supported with the tools, trust and opportunities to grow your way.

The School of Engineering is inviting applications for a Doctoral Researcher in Physics-Enhanced Machine Learning for Floating Offshore Wind Digital Twins Floating offshore wind turbines will be central to the clean-energy transition, but their behaviour at sea is difficult to predict and monitor. They move in six degrees of freedom under irregular waves and turbulent wind. The mooring lines that keep them in position are located deep underwater, where permanent sensing is costly and difficult to maintain. Operators therefore need digital twins that combine hydrodynamic knowledge with sensor data to estimate quantities that cannot be measured directly. In this full-time, salaried Doctoral Researcher position, you will help develop the next generation of these digital twins: models that capture the wave-driven dynamics of floating turbines, update as new data arrive, detect early signs of degradation, and quantify the uncertainty of their estimates. The position is funded by the Research Council of Finland. It is based at Aalto University's Otaniemi campus in Espoo, Finland, and starts on 28 January 2027 or as agreed. Research environment and duties At the Department of Energy and Mechanical Engineering, our Marine and Arctic Technology research group studies how ships and offshore structures move and are loaded in waves, wind and ice. We combine machine learning and data-driven methods with hydrodynamic theory, numerical simulation and model-scale experiments. In this role, you will help us build digital twins that track the wave-induced motions, mooring loads and structural condition of floating offshore wind turbines in real time using only a small number of sensors. Your work will contribute to safer and more cost-effective floating wind farms, where wave loads and mooring tensions can be monitored continuously, degradation can be detected early, and maintenance can be planned before failures occur. Your work will include: Developing physics-enhanced machine-learning models that learn the coupled hydrodynamic and structural dynamics of floating wind turbines from measured data and update in real time. These methods will build on, among other approaches, Koopman operator theory and dynamic mode decomposition (DMD). Embedding hydrodynamic knowledge into these models so that they remain physically consistent across sea states, including wave excitation, radiation-memory effects, slow-drift motions and mooring-line dynamics. Estimating wave-induced motions and mooring loads that cannot be measured directly. Detecting early mooring-system or structural degradation and distinguishing it from normal changes in waves, wind and turbine operating conditions. Quantifying the uncertainty of these estimates using Bayesian filtering and probabilistic machine learning. Generating and analysing data from: hydrodynamic simulations, including potential-flow methods and, where needed, computational fluid dynamics (CFD) and coupled simulation tools such as OpenFAST Publishing results in leading international journals and presenting them at conferences. You will work closely with researchers in the Marine and Arctic Technology group and with our international academic collaborators. This is an exciting time to join us. Floating offshore wind is scaling up rapidly, and industry guidance increasingly favours indirect monitoring of hard-to-access components, such as mooring lines, using sensors located elsewhere on the structure. Our group has recently shown that digital twins learned directly from measurements can estimate unmeasured responses and loads from only a few sensors, including verification using wave-basin test data. In this role, you will take these methods a step further by embedding hydrodynamics into the learning process and moving from accurate estimation toward reliable, self-updating condition monitoring. What you bring To thrive in this role, you will need: A Master's degree completed by the start of the position. Suitable backgrounds include naval architecture, marine or ocean engineering, offshore engineering, mechanical, civil or aerospace engineering, applied mathematics, physics, computer science, or a related field. A strong foundation in linear algebra and in at least one of the following areas: hydrodynamics or fluid mechanics, structural dynamics, dynamical systems, or signal processing. Good programming skills in Python or a similar language, together with a genuine interest in machine learning. Curiosity, independence, and the ability to communicate clearly and work well in a team. We also value: Knowledge of marine or offshore hydrodynamics, such as wave-structure interaction, potential-flow or boundary-element methods, or computational fluid dynamics (e.g. OpenFOAM or REEF3D). Experience with OpenFAST, MoorDyn or WAMIT, or similar software. Experience with dynamic mode decomposition, Koopman operator methods, system identification or operational modal analysis. Experience with Kalman filtering, Bayesian inference, Gaussian processes or uncertainty quantification. Experience with deep learning for time series, such as Transformers or graph neural networks, using PyTorch or JAX. Scientific publications or a strong Master's thesis in a related area.
